added.title: Timeline page on a ts-ordered index
added.summary: Serve timelinePage's window statements and the more-probe from an index ordered by ts, with no temp B-tree, pinned by EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN.
added.objective: Close epic criterion 38e415f2 (verdict-v3 gap 1). timelinePage (factory/orchestrator/src/db/queries.ts) runs one window statement per loop: rows matching scopeConditions (event_type IN the page types, the session scope, the task id), the cursor bounds and the strict lastTs bound, ordered by ts DESC (a before page) or ASC (an after page), LIMIT limit + 1. A full window is followed by a tie-group completion statement on ts = tieTs. ui/server's more-probe reaches the same code as a before page with limit 1. Today SQLite plans the window statement as `SEARCH events_raw USING INDEX events_raw_type_idx (event_type=?)` plus `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`, so it reads every timeline-type row, payload included, into a sorter before the LIMIT applies. Make SQLite serve the window statement in both directions, the tie-group completion and the more-probe from an index ordered by ts. Each must read O(limit) rows and must not use a temp B-tree. Choose the shape from the query and prove it with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN against the real migrated schema. One planner probe, on a table shaped like events_raw, suggests three things. A unary plus on the event_type term (`+event_type IN (...)`) moves the unscoped page onto the existing events_raw_ts_idx with no temp B-tree. A composite (event_type, ts) or (ts, event_type) index on its own leaves the planner on type_idx. A session-scoped page needs a (session_id, ts) shaped index to lose its temp B-tree. Treat these as hints to confirm or refute, not as the answer. The fix stays inside the window statements: the load-all path (no limit) and pagedEpicMatcher share scopeConditions, and neither may lose its type_idx plan. A new index with a drizzle migration is allowed; this lifts task-13's no-new-index clause. If one is added, it is migration 0018, generated by drizzle-kit together with its journal entry and snapshot, and schema.ts declares it. Then pin the result at the SQLite level, which task-13's tests did not do: a test captures the statements timelinePage actually prepares and asserts their query plan.

functional_clauses: Every window statement timelinePage prepares is served by an index ordered by ts, reads O(limit) rows, and plans with no `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`. That covers the limit + 1 window in both directions and the ts = tieTs tie-group completion, and so also the ui/server more-probe, which is a before page with limit 1.

The change is confined to those statements. The load-all timeline path, pagedEpicMatcher's pre-pass and every other events_raw reader keep their current plans: no `SEARCH ... events_raw_type_idx` becomes a full `SCAN events_raw`.
Page content, order, cursor semantics and tie handling are unchanged. The existing parity, paging and cursor tests are the contract for that and stay green.

If an index is added, it lands as a single drizzle migration, 0018, generated by drizzle-kit. No drizzle config file exists, so pass the dialect, schema and output folder on the command line, the way 0017 was produced. The migration includes its meta/_journal.json entry and meta/0018_snapshot.json, schema.ts declares the same index, and the SQL file holds only CREATE INDEX statements. If no index is needed, no migration file is written, and the Result says so.

A new test, factory/orchestrator/test/db/timelinePlan.test.ts, pins the plan at the SQLite level. It uses the statements and parameters that timelinePage really prepares, captured at the driver; a hand-copied SQL string does not count. It comes with a revert proof.
nonfunctional_clauses: Work is proven by query plan or by counts, never by timing; no test asserts a duration.
keeps_exports: no export of queries.ts is removed or has its declaration changed. ui/server consumes it.
ui/server imports the orchestrator's dist, so run `pnpm run build` and then `pnpm run test:server` as well as the orchestrator suite.

Edit only the claimed files; a needed edit outside them stops the task with error.spec.spec-gap. Under factory/orchestrator/drizzle/, only the new 0018 files and the new journal entry are written. No existing migration or snapshot is ever edited.
The migration, if any, applies cleanly to an existing store at the previous schema (0017), and the existing tests that run the migrator stay green.
Do not rely on ANALYZE or sqlite_stat1: production runs neither, so the plan must hold on a store with no statistics.
A generated drizzle meta snapshot is about 1,800 lines and counts toward diff_lines; the budget allows for one.
In the worktree, node_modules is a symlink to the main clone's; stage files by name and never run `git add -A`.
English only; no absolute paths and no other project names; fixtures use neutral names (project-a, project-b, epic-a, epic-b, store-a, store-b, demo-hub, blacksmith).
Tests build their fixtures in temp dirs and read no git history.
Run the matching typecheck scripts and `pnpm run lint`, then `bash scripts/check.sh` in full as the final gate; quote its tail and name every SKIP.

acceptance_criteria: Epic criterion 11 (38e415f2): a limit-8 page is read by an ORDER BY ts LIMIT 9 statement that an index serves. timelinePlan.test.ts builds a store in a temp dir with the real migrations and captures the SQL and parameters timelinePage prepares for four calls: an unscoped before page (limit 8), an after page, the more-probe (a before cursor with limit 1) and a window full enough to trigger the tie-group completion. It runs EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on each captured statement and asserts three things about every plan: its detail rows name an index whose ordering column is ts (events_raw_ts_idx, or the new index), it contains no `USE TEMP B-TREE`, and it does not name events_raw_type_idx. The Result pastes each plan. Revert proof: with the fix reverted, the test fails and names type_idx and the temp B-tree; paste both outputs.

Rows read do not grow with history. The same test builds stores at N and 10N timeline rows (N at least 2,000) and asserts that the captured plans are identical at both sizes. A deterministic rows-read count is an acceptable additional instrument, for example the driver's statement counters if the bundled SQLite exposes them, or a fixture whose rows read can be derived exactly. Timing is not acceptable.

Nothing else regresses. The Result pastes EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN before and after the change for the load-all timeline path (no limit) and for pagedEpicMatcher's pre-pass; neither turns a SEARCH on events_raw_type_idx into a full SCAN events_raw. It also pastes the plans of the session-scoped page variants (one session id and a session id list) and the task-scoped variant. Each of those either has no temp B-tree, or the Result states the residual exactly: rows read are bounded by that session's or that task's own timeline rows, not by the store's.

timelineCost.test.ts, timelinePaging.test.ts (including its cursor and tie tests) and timelineParity.test.ts stay green, and their assertions are not weakened; quote the pass counts. If a migration was added, three more things hold. A test opens a temp-dir store migrated to 0017, runs the migrator, and shows the new index in sqlite_master. Every existing test that runs the migrator stays green. `git diff --stat` shows no edit to any existing file under factory/orchestrator/drizzle/ except the one new _journal.json entry.

`pnpm run build`, `pnpm run test`, `pnpm run test:server`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test` and `pnpm run lint` pass, then `bash scripts/check.sh` runs in full. The Result quotes its tail and names every SKIP.

added.title: Overview poll with bounded work
added.summary: Memoise overview's projection stage until the projection advances, recompute only the clock stage per poll from indexed reads, and route /api/projects and /api/sessions through the memo.
added.objective: Close epic criterion a2da2311 (verdict-v3 gap 2). Today every Home poll repeats whole-history work, for three reasons. First, ui/server/src/app.ts's sharedOverview memo is keyed on the refresher generation plus data_version, but an entry also expires at `overviewMemo.maxAgeMs ?? 4000`, which is shorter than PULSE_POLL_MS = 5000, so every poll recomputes. Second, /api/projects and /api/sessions (the all-stores path and the scoped path) call overview() directly and bypass the memo. Third, overview() itself does whole-history work: it JSON.parses every task-result-recorded row (taskResultRows) and every registry and task-added row up to the 5 min and 1 h cutoffs (liveAgentsAt, tokensSpentAt, tokensBudgetedAt); it reads the whole dispatches table to keep the newest ten; and runningSessions finds each session's newest event with `(session_id, ts) IN (SELECT session_id, max(ts) ... GROUP BY session_id)`, a full scan. Split the work into two stages. The projection stage holds everything that changes only when the projection advances; app.ts memoises it per (store, scope), keyed on projection state alone, with no age bound. The clock stage holds only what depends on now: working and stalled agent counts, idle and actively running epics, per-project working counts and idle epics, runningSessions' working counts, liveAgentCountDelta5m, workingAgentCountDelta5m and budgetUsedPctPointDelta1h. It is recomputed per poll from the memoised stage plus indexed reads whose rows are bounded by the clock windows and the live agents, not by history. One way to bound the deltas: the spend an hour ago is the spend now minus the measured spend in task-result-recorded rows with ts after the cutoff. Whatever method is used, its output must match today's fold, and the overviewDeltas tests decide that. overview(db, scope, opts) keeps its signature and returns the same result, built from the two stages. /api/overview, /api/active-scope, /api/projects and /api/sessions all read the shared memo. runningSessions' newest-event read becomes index-served: one indexed lookup per session, from an index whose leading columns are (session_id, ts), or from a column the projector already maintains. The newest-ten dispatches read becomes an ORDER BY with a LIMIT that an index serves. The parses of task-result-recorded, registry and task-added rows become incremental or window-bounded. Indexes this needs land as migration 0019 (task-19 may have taken 0018). First read what task-19 added, and reuse an index that already serves. Residual, stated exactly and allowed by the epic criterion's 'or a result memoised until the projection advances': when the projection does advance, epicActivityRows (a json_extract GROUP BY), sessionProjects and sessionTitles may still read whole history inside SQLite, once per advance. /api/sessions/:sessionId/agents is out of scope.

functional_clauses: overview() is built from two stages. The projection stage depends only on projection state, and the clock stage depends on now. overview(db, scope, opts) keeps its signature and its result: for any store and any nowIso it returns what it returns today. New exports for the stages are allowed. No existing export is removed or changes its declaration.

app.ts memoises the projection stage per (store, scope), keyed on the refresher generation plus data_version, with no age bound. A poll with no projection advance reruns only the clock stage. `overviewMemo.maxAgeMs` no longer ends an entry; the option may stay as an accepted, ignored field, or go if nothing else reads it.

/api/overview, /api/active-scope, /api/projects and /api/sessions (both its all-stores path and its scoped path) all read through the shared memo, so one Home poll computes the projection stage at most once per (store, scope).

The clock stage reads only rows bounded by the clock windows and the live agents: the 5 min and 1 h windows, read by index on ts, plus the live agents. Its output for every clock-dependent field equals today's, including liveAgentCountDelta5m, workingAgentCountDelta5m and budgetUsedPctPointDelta1h.

runningSessions' per-session newest-event read is served by an index, one lookup per session, with no full `SCAN events_raw` and no temp B-tree. The newest-ten dispatches read is an ORDER BY with a LIMIT that an index serves, plus at most one tie group, and keeps today's tie-break order. The task-result-recorded, registry and task-added parses are incremental or bounded by the clock windows.

Any index this needs is added in schema.ts and lands as a single drizzle migration, 0019, generated by drizzle-kit together with its meta/_journal.json entry and meta/0019_snapshot.json. The SQL file holds only CREATE INDEX statements. If task-19 already added an index that serves, it is reused, not duplicated.
nonfunctional_clauses: Work is proven by counts or query plan, never by timing; no test asserts a duration.
keeps_exports: no export of queries.ts is removed or has its declaration changed. ui/server consumes it. Adding exports is allowed.
ui/server imports the orchestrator's dist, so run `pnpm run build` and then `pnpm run test:server` as well as the orchestrator suite.

Edit only the claimed files; a needed edit outside them stops the task with error.spec.spec-gap. overviewDeltas, overviewIdle, workingAgents and runningSessionsLastStep tests are not claimed: they must stay green unedited. Under factory/orchestrator/drizzle/, only the new 0019 files and the new journal entry are written. No existing migration or snapshot is ever edited.
The migration applies cleanly to an existing store at the previous schema (0018 if task-19 added one, else 0017), and the existing tests that run the migrator stay green.
Do not rely on ANALYZE or sqlite_stat1: production runs neither, so plans must hold on a store with no statistics.
A generated drizzle meta snapshot is about 1,800 lines and counts toward diff_lines; the budget allows for one.
In the worktree, node_modules is a symlink to the main clone's; stage files by name and never run `git add -A`.
English only; no absolute paths and no other project names; fixtures use neutral names (project-a, project-b, epic-a, epic-b, store-a, store-b, demo-hub, blacksmith).
Tests build their fixtures in temp dirs and read no git history.
Run the matching typecheck scripts and `pnpm run lint`, then `bash scripts/check.sh` in full as the final gate; quote its tail and name every SKIP.

acceptance_criteria: Epic criterion 12 (a2da2311): per-poll database work is close to constant. A new test, factory/orchestrator/test/db/overviewPoll.test.ts, builds two stores in temp dirs from the real migrations: one at N events of history and one at 10N (N at least 2,000), with the same live agents and the same activity inside the clock windows. For a repeat poll with the injected clock moved 5 s forward and no new event, it counts four things: projection-stage computations, which must be 0; payload JSON.parse calls; rows the clock stage reads from events_raw; and rows it reads from dispatches. All four counts are equal at N and 10N. The Result pastes the counts. Revert proof: on today's code the parse count grows with N; paste both runs. Counts only, no timing.

After one appended event and a projection advance, the incremental parses are bounded. In the same test, the payload parses of task-result-recorded, registry and task-added rows are bounded by the appended events plus the rows inside the 5 min and 1 h windows, and are equal at N and 10N. The newest-ten dispatches read returns at most RECENT_DISPATCHES_LIMIT + 1 rows plus one tie group, keeps today's tie-break (shown by a test of a burst of dispatches inside one millisecond), and its EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows no full SCAN dispatches and no temp B-tree. If the residual named in the objective remains (epicActivityRows, sessionProjects and sessionTitles reading whole history in SQLite once per advance), the Result states it with file:line.

runningSessions is index-served. The test captures runningSessions' newest-event statement and runs EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on it. The plan shows no `SCAN events_raw` other than through an index lookup per session, and no `USE TEMP B-TREE`. Its output is unchanged: runningSessionsLastStep.test.ts stays green unedited. The Result pastes the plan before and after.

The routes share the memo. ui/server/test/overviewShared.test.ts counts projection-stage computations; the pass-through mock is re-pointed from overview() to the stage export, and that change is stated in the Result. One poll that requests /api/overview, /api/active-scope, /api/projects and /api/sessions, both scoped and all-stores, computes the projection stage once per (store, scope). A repeat poll after the injected clock passes PULSE_POLL_MS with no projection advance computes it 0 times, and the clock-dependent fields still reflect the new clock. The old test 'recomputes each store once the bound has passed' is rewritten to that new contract. The Result names it, and every other rewritten test, with its old and new intent. The remaining overviewShared tests stay green, including 'recomputes only the store whose projection advanced' and 'keeps different scopes apart'.

Nothing else regresses. overviewCost.test.ts stays green with its assertions not weakened. overviewDeltas, overviewIdle, workingAgents and runningSessionsLastStep tests stay green unedited. Quote the pass counts. The migration test opens a temp-dir store at the previous schema, runs the migrator, and shows the new indexes in sqlite_master. `git diff --stat` shows no edit to any existing file under factory/orchestrator/drizzle/ except the one new _journal.json entry.

`pnpm run build`, `pnpm run test`, `pnpm run test:server`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test`, `pnpm run typecheck:server` and `pnpm run lint` pass, then `bash scripts/check.sh` runs in full. The Result quotes its tail and names every SKIP.
